solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kind of place with supply of trees

definitions.text: Kind of place with supply of trees

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb of supple, so the letters bend flexibly into a new order

blocks.note: to pin is to place or fix something, as in pinning the tail on the donkey
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone describes a spot that keeps a stock of trees, as if it were a nursery or depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun meaning stock, but it is the adverb from supple. The whole clue also serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest of conifers of one genus is literally a location holding a great many trees of one kind.

clue.text: Fairy liquid initially removed from bottle

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word liquid, which is the letter to be taken out
removed from tells us that a letter is taken out of the following word

blocks.note: the first letter of liquid
bottle is British slang for courage, which is pluck

explanation.surface: A sprite's washing-up liquid has been taken out of its bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy liquid' reads as the British washing-up liquid brand, but Fairy is the definition. PLUCK minus L gives PUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite of English folklore, best known from A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: In reporter's role, cut grass with sailor

definitions.note: a phrase describing activity; the answer is the present participle

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word for grass loses its final letter

blocks.note: a nark is an informer; to grass is to inform
a rating is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A journalist on assignment mows the lawn alongside a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut grass' looks like lawn mowing, but grass is an informer here, and cut docks that word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone telling a story in the role of a reporter is recounting events, which is what narrating means.

clue.text: Judas seen here appropriately!

blocks.note: surface reading: the disciple who betrayed Jesus, a byword for any traitor
setter's reading: this entry sits in the grid's fifth vertical line of squares, so the traitor is literally placed in that position

explanation.surface: A remark that the arch-betrayer is fittingly found right here.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry starts on the fifth letter of 1 across, so it runs down the fifth column of the grid: the traitor's label describes where it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth columnist is a traitor working from within, and Judas is the archetypal betrayer.

clue.text: Part of the tale reader's about to tell

indicators.note: part of signals that the letters lie within a run of the clue's words
about means turned around, so the run is read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the, all of tale and the start of reader

explanation.surface: Someone is about to recount a piece of the story a reader is telling.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'thE TALE Reader' backwards gives RELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: College not halved?

blocks.note: semi- is the prefix for half
nary is a dialect word for not, as in nary a one

explanation.surface: A question whether a college has avoided being cut in two.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in the opposite order to the clue: halved, then not. The question mark flags the loose wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college that trains priests or ministers.

clue.text: Most of tag team seen in old sitcom

indicators.note: most of means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the word tag without its last letter
a team of eleven players, as in cricket or football, is written XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Most of a tag-team wrestling pair appears in a vintage TV comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi was an American sitcom set in a New York cab company, first aired in 1978.

clue.text: District around northern stadium

indicators.note: around means placed so as to surround, so one word encloses a letter

blocks.note: an area is a district
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood surrounds a football ground in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or entertainment, much like a stadium.

clue.text: I had to feed friendly cow

indicators.note: feeding something puts it inside, so these letters go into the next word

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
intimate means close and friendly

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having to give fodder to a docile cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal from the farmyard surface but is a verb meaning to browbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, the same as to bully or overawe them.

clue.text: An American whips the Marine into shape

indicators.note: whipping something into shape means forcing it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these words

explanation.surface: A US drill sergeant licks a Marine recruit into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whips' reads as the verb of the drill sergeant, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Hampshirite is a native or resident of the US state of New Hampshire, hence an American.

clue.text: Sensible judge – cracking old headdress

indicators.note: cracking something open lets one thing break into another, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a referee, or ref, judges a match
a caul was a close-fitting netted cap worn by women in former times

explanation.surface: A level-headed judge breaks open an antique hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful person is prudent and cautious, which is to say sensible.

clue.text: An inflatable sheep found in Spar

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the sheep word sits within the other

blocks.note: a ewe is a female sheep
a spar is a pole such as a ship's mast

explanation.surface: A blow-up sheep turns up in a Spar shop, a British convenience-store chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is capitalised to suggest the grocery chain; here it is a ship's pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mae West is an RAF inflatable life jacket, nicknamed after the buxom film star.

clue.text: As sexy nurses can get married, it's stimulating

definitions.note: a description of a thing; the answer is a noun phrase for a stimulus

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close and cradle, so the word for sexy encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
hot means sexy
a tin is a can
to get a message is to hear it, as in I get you
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Attractive nurses who are able to wed find it exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' reads as hospital staff but is a verb meaning holds. To get something can mean to hear it, as in 'I get you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the arm is an idiom for a boost or tonic, something that invigorates.

clue.text: Criminal breezed in carrying new drug

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters that follow are bent into a new order
carrying means holding within, so the rearranged letters take one in

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A crook strolled in with a fresh supply of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzedrine is a trade name for amphetamine, a stimulant drug.

clue.text: Absence of viewpoint about inventor

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: absence of something means there is no such thing
a side of an argument is a viewpoint

explanation.surface: Someone without an opinion is concerned with an inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Filling in part of puzzle, staff didn't look happy

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so the staff word sits within the puzzle part

blocks.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
the grid is the part of a crossword where answers are written

explanation.surface: Office workers completing a section of the crossword looked glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees doing the crossword, but it is a ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to twist the face in pain or disgust, the opposite of looking pleased.

clue.text: C+ secures position as President

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the outer letters wrap another word

blocks.note: C taken as written, and the plus sign read as the word and
a level is a position or rank on a scale

explanation.surface: A middling C-plus grade is enough to land someone the presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: C+ looks like a school grade; read it aloud as 'C and' and put LEVEL between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland served twice as US President, in the 1880s and 1890s.

clue.text: Done with butter, I'll make beef slices

blocks.note: something done with is past or over
a ram is an animal that butts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook says that once finished with the butter, they will prepare sliced beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked beef, usually served thinly sliced.

clue.text: Snake cut in half by gunners in empty tower

indicators.note: cutting a word in half keeps only one of its two halves
in means placed inside, so the gunners go within the word for empty

blocks.note: to snake is to zigzag
to gut something is to empty it
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A serpent is sliced in two by soldiers in a deserted tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty tower' looks like one phrase, but empty belongs to the wordplay and tower alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ziggurat is a stepped pyramid-shaped temple tower of ancient Mesopotamia.

clue.text: A track's climbing

blocks.note: taken as written
a scent is a trail or track followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A path is heading uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is the act of going up, so a noun for climbing.

clue.text: Chased by police, sped off

indicators.note: being chased by someone means they come behind, so the police letters are placed after

blocks.note: ran is a past tense meaning sped
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A suspect pursued by the cops raced away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sped off' looks like one phrase, but off alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is rotten or rank, the same as rancid butter.

clue.text: Affectionate wizard's fight to hold on

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so the fight word wraps around another

blocks.note: a demon at something is a wizard at it, a whizz
to strive is to struggle or fight
at and on both mark a location, as in at or on the coast

explanation.surface: A loving sorcerer struggles to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase meaning persevere; split it so the struggle word holds a small word meaning on. At and on both mark position.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative person openly shows feelings, which is to say they are warmly affectionate.

clue.text: Mysterious soldier in raincoat

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the soldier goes within the coat

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
a mac, short for mackintosh, is a British word for a raincoat

explanation.surface: An enigmatic soldier stands wrapped in his waterproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic as an adjective means having uncanny, supernatural power, hence mysterious.

clue.text: Seductress denied one time

indicators.note: denied means refused or deprived of, so the letter for one is withheld

blocks.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of Islamic paradise, hence a voluptuous temptress
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A temptress was turned down once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one time' reads as 'once', but one belongs to the wordplay and time alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time, sixty minutes long.

clue.text: Food eaten by fool, you might say

indicators.note: you might say tells us to go by how a phrase is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: by can mean in, and a fool is a jester; together they are spoken like the answer

explanation.surface: A meal consumed by a clown, as one might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and wordplay share the idea of eating: food eaten is literally inside the jester.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesta is the technical term for material taken into the body as nourishment.

clue.text: Type of bridge in a pass

blocks.note: something in is fashionable, or chic
taken as written
a pass at something is a try, or a go

explanation.surface: A sort of bridge spans a mountain gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' and 'pass' paint a mountain road, but bridge is the card game and pass is an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a form of contract bridge played as four-deal rubbers, a variety of the card game.

clue.text: A head teacher's part

indicators.note: part means a portion of the word, so the letters lie within it

blocks.note: the letters inside the word teacher

explanation.surface: A head teacher has a role to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head teacher' reads as one title; split it so A head is the definition and the 's is short for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices given as so much each are charged per person, that is per head.

clue.text: Face worker protecting awful psychic

indicators.note: protecting means guarding by surrounding, so the worker's letters enclose another word

blocks.note: a miner works at the coal face
dread as an adjective means dreadful or awful

explanation.surface: A labourer shields a dreadful clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' suggests a human face; it is the coalface where miners dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind reader claims telepathic power to know others' thoughts, a kind of psychic.
